criterion: conformance.report sorts Codex and hook sessions on one comparable value, and _overlaps needs no type filter to avoid inventing an overlap
summary: The attempt-1 failure re-derived independently, read-only and metadata-only: 137 rows, median span 353s, max 2,041,985s = 23.63 days, 13 over a day. Reviewer then corrected its own earlier scoping: _codex_verdicts filters subagents and 108 of the 137 are subagents, so over rows that actually become verdicts it is 5 of 29 contesting, with 9 of 29 windows exceeding a day. The defect stands at the correct scope. Four reviewer-built fixtures confirm the fix: the 23.6-day window around a 30-second conformant session leaves both uncontested; two genuinely observed overlapping sessions are both contested; two overlapping Codex rows are not; and different repositories stay separate. Design judged sound rather than a band-aid: bounding the window would fabricate an end time the store does not contain, dropping the timestamps would forfeit the sorting objective, and excluding-and-labelling keeps the true data while declining the unsupported inference. Placement in conformance.py defended as part of the versioned verdict shape, and grep confirms no consumer outside the module reads contested or bounds. SCHEMA_VERSION 3 checked: nothing reads the old shape and effectiveness.report's embedded block carries no per-session data, so correctly not bumped.
